question.problem:
For the vector $u=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ -2\end{aligned}]$ which of the following statements are true?

I. $u⊥H,\,$ where $H=\{[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 10 \\ 1\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 10 \\ 5\end{aligned}]\}$

II. $u⊥V,\,$ where $V=\{[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 10 \\ -1\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 10 \\ -5\end{aligned}]\}$

III. $u⊥W,\,$ where $W=\{[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 0 \\ 5\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}10 \\ -5 \\ 0\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 10 \\ -1\end{aligned}]\}$
question.worked_solution:
Let's denote the vectors of $H,V$ and $W$ as $\{{h}_{1},{h}_{2}\},\{{v}_{1},{v}_{2}\}$ and $\{{w}_{1},{w}_{2},{w}_{3}\}$, respectively.  

Now, we have to compute the dot product between $u$ and the vectors in each set. 

- For the set $H:$

$$
\begin{aligned}u\cdot {h}_{1} & =2\cdot (-4)+1\cdot 10+(-2)\cdot 1=0 & ✓ \\ u\cdot {h}_{2} & =2\cdot 0+1\cdot 10+(-2)\cdot 5=0 & ✓\end{aligned}
$$

So, $u⊥H.$

- For the set $V:$

$$
\begin{aligned}u\cdot {v}_{1} & =2\cdot (-4)+1\cdot 10+(-2)\cdot (-1)=4\ne 0 & \times  \\ u\cdot {v}_{2} & =2\cdot 0+1\cdot 10+(-2)\cdot (-5)=20\ne 0 & \times \end{aligned}
$$

So, $u⊥̸V.$

- For the set $W:$

$$
\begin{aligned}u\cdot {w}_{1} & =2\cdot 5+1\cdot 0+(-2)\cdot 5=0 & ✓ \\ u\cdot {w}_{2} & =2\cdot 10+1\cdot (-5)+(-2)\cdot 0=15\ne 0 & \times  \\ u\cdot {w}_{3} & =2\cdot (-4)+1\cdot 10+(-2)\cdot (-1)=4\ne 0 & \times \end{aligned}
$$

So, $u⊥̸W.$

Therefore, the correct answer is "I only."
